# `progress` is measured against `max`, and each platform's widget wants that
# expressed in its own units.
#
# GTK's fraction and Compose's progress are both 0..1, so a platform that
# passes `value` straight through renders 2-of-10 as a full bar. HTML's
# <progress> takes both numbers, so it does not divide -- but max="0" is not
# valid there either.
#
# The shared cause was `max` having no default and rendering as its zero value.
# It defaults to 1, which is the value HTML's element already assumes and the
# only one that leaves value/max meaning what it says.

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=h app.sngl
grep '<progress max="10" value="2">' h/index.html
grep '<progress max="1" value="0.5">' h/index.html
! grep 'max="0"' h/index.html

sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --opt=gir=builtin --out=g app.sngl
# 2 of 10 is a fifth of the bar, not all of it.
grep 'set_fraction\(.*C\.double\(0\.2\)\)' g/model.go
grep 'set_fraction\(.*C\.double\(0\.5\)\)' g/model.go

sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=a app.sngl
grep 'LinearProgressIndicator\(progress = \{ \(2\.0 / 10\.0\)\.toFloat\(\) \}' a/MainScreen.kt

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component main {
    window(title="t") {
        progress(value=2.0, max=10.0)
        progress(value=0.5)
    }
}
